subject: Throughput surge & rate/overage terms — post-call recap and options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@veridiant.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@veridiant.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Throughput surge & rate/overage terms — post-call recap and options

Hi Liam / Priya — great talking earlier. Quick recap from our call + suggested next steps so we have a shared record.

Key points you shared
- Baseline generation traffic: ~120M tokens/month (text gen + chat).
- Occasional product launches with sharp peaks (estimated single-day peak up to ~1B tokens; multi-hour surges ~3-6 hours).
- Primary concerns: predictable monthly spend, protecting against runaway burst costs, and a straightforward overage cap for finance.

Requested from you
- Confirmation of a typical monthly budget range (ballpark is fine)
- Any procurement constraints / legal timeline we should target

Our recommended options (high level) — attached a detailed pricing grid: 20260120-Redwood-pricing-grid.pdf
1) Committed tier + controlled surge allowance (recommended for predictable spend)
   - Example pilot: 250M committed tokens / month for 3 months.
   - Target unit econ: $650 per 1M tokens on committed volume.
   - Surge allowance: 2x daily average (soft surge bucket) with automatic prefix caching/ batching to reduce cost.
   - Overage (if allowance exceeded): $1,200 per 1M tokens, with 2x soft-throttle after 1.5x baseline to protect downstream systems.

2) On-demand with budget guardrails (if you can't commit yet)
   - Standard hosted rates for on-demand usage; configurable burst hard-cap and pre-set notification thresholds.
   - Option to set a hard daily or hourly cap enforced by our routing layer; overage billed monthly at premium rate.

3) Dedicated pool (for launches / long-term heavy usage)
   - Reserved capacity, predictable throughput, ability to carve out launch windows.

Action items
- Liam/Priya: confirm a target monthly budget range (e.g., $60k–$90k) and whether the procurement team needs a signed disposition before pilot.
- Redwood: prepare MAP and a short contract example (see attached MAP spreadsheet).

Attachments: 20260114-Veridiant-MAP.xlsx, 20260120-Redwood-pricing-grid.pdf

If helpful, we can sketch a conservative pilot agreement that caps exposure (e.g., daily hard cap + monthly overage ceiling) while giving you runway to test bursts. Suggest a 30–45 minute follow-up next week to lock the numbers.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]
[Attachment: 20260114-Veridiant-MAP.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@veridiant.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@veridiant.com>, procurement@veridiant.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Throughput surge & rate/overage terms — post-call recap and options

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Volumes: baseline is accurate (~120M/mo). During product launches we see concentrated traffic windows where traffic can hit ~1B tokens over a 3–6 hour window; those are business critical and we need to keep the UX consistent.

2) Budget: finance is targeting an upper bound of $75k/mo for this initiative initially (we could stretch to $90k for a short promo/launch month). That said, finance will push back on surprises — any overage needs a hard ceiling or pre-approval flow.

3) Overage protection: we like the idea of a daily hard cap + a soft surge allowance. Can you propose an overage $/1M that is tolerable but not punitive? If the overage rate is > $1,000/1M we will likely push back. Also want a 2-week notice window for any committed quota increases that would affect billing.

4) Timeline: procurement wants a 2–3 week review cycle for legal and SLA items. If Redwood can provide a draft that includes a clear overage cap and an emergency rollback clause, it will speed review.

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up Monday if you can do it.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Product Operations | Veridiant
liam.oconnor@veridiant.com
[Attachment: none]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@veridiant.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@veridiant.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput surge & rate/overage terms — post-call recap and options

Thanks Liam — really helpful. Quick note inline to your asks and a concrete pilot proposal so Procurement has something tangible to review.

Inline:
- Overage target: we can start with $1,100 per 1M tokens as our standard overage price for on-demand; however in pilot/committed scenarios we can negotiate down to $1,000/1M as a capped emergency rate.
- 2-week notice for quota increases: yes, we can include a clause that requires 14 calendar days' notice for committing to a new baseline that would affect billing. For emergency increases (e.g., live launch), we support one-off temporary surge windows under a pre-approved MA clause.

Proposed pilot (recommended) — see attached pricing grid for math: 20260120-Redwood-pricing-grid.pdf
- Term: 3 months
- Committed: 250M tokens / month
- Committed price: $650 / 1M tokens (applies to committed bucket)
- Surge allowance: up to 2x daily average as a soft burst bucket (auto-applied; Redwood will throttle progressively after 1.5x baseline to protect your budget and upstream systems)
- Overage pricing (capped): $1,000 / 1M tokens (billing cap we can include in pilot contract)
- Hard cap option: we will configure a monthly hard spend cap that stops generation if hit — Finance can set this in the console.

Why this structure: it gives Veridiant predictable unit economics on committed usage while protecting against surprise spend during big launches. We will also enable prefix/KV caching for high-volume launch patterns to materially reduce token consumption.

Next steps
1) Jordan/Marissa: prepare a two-page pilot summary + MAP and a contract skeleton with the $1,000/1M overage cap and 14-day quota notice. (I will attach these by EOD Tuesday.)
2) Veridiant: confirm procurement contact (procurement@veridiant.com is copied) and whether procurement prefers DocuSign or a PDF + email signature.
3) Set a follow-up call: propose Tue 20-Jan or Wed 21-Jan 30-min slot.

Thanks — I’ll loop Legal/Contracts once you confirm procurement preference.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: 20260120-Redwood-pricing-grid.pdf (PDF)]

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@veridiant.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@veridiant.com>
Cc: procurement@veridiant.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 14:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Throughput surge & rate/overage terms — post-call recap and options

Jordan — thanks. Procurement prefers DocuSign for speed. A few quick asks from Legal/Finance before we sign:

- Can Redwood make the overage cap $1,000 / 1M tokens (pilot) and keep an escalation path if we exceed that frequently?
- Include a 14-day notice clause for quota baseline increases that affect billing.
- Add a monthly overage ceiling (e.g., no more than 30% over committed spend without explicit approval) and an emergency rollback clause for launches that go sideways.

If you can fold those into the pilot skeleton and send via DocuSign, procurement will start review immediately. We aim for a 2–3 week review cycle.

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
VP, Finance | Veridiant
procurement@veridiant.com
[Attachment: none]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jan 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Throughput surge & rate/overage terms — post-call recap and options

Marissa / Neha — forwarding the thread after Priya's confirmation. Procurement wants DocuSign + the following guardrails:
- Pilot: 3 months, 250M committed / month at $650 / 1M on committed volume
- Surge allowance: 2x soft burst; progressive throttling after 1.5x baseline
- Overage cap: $1,000 / 1M (pilot)
- Monthly overage ceiling: no more than 30% over committed spend without explicit approval
- 14-day notice for baseline increases

Can Legal/Contracts draft a DocuSign-ready pilot skeleton that includes the above and an emergency rollback clause? I believe we can give the client the $1,000/1M overage cap for the pilot to get this moving. Please flag any risks — deal_id VER-2026-004.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-sla-digest.pdf (PDF)]
